```js
    path.join(PKG_DIR, 'O8.5-S4-compressed-deflateraw.js')
  ];
  for (const f of allFiles) {
    execSync(`node -c "${f}"`, { stdio: 'pipe' });
  }
  report(1, 'Syntax Validation (node -c across all sources and deliverables)', true, `${allFiles.length} files verified clean`);
} catch (e) {
  report(1, 'Syntax Validation', false, e.message);
}

// 2. Clean Shard Term Hygiene
try {
  const forbidden = ['GoogleUnlock', 'camo', 'decoy', 'Companion', 'Retention', 'typedPool'];
  let violations = [];
  for (const f of fs.readdirSync(SHARDS_DIR)) {
    const content = fs.readFileSync(path.join(SHARDS_DIR, f), 'utf8');
    for (const term of forbidden) {
      if (content.includes(term)) {
        violations.push(`${f}:${term}`);
      }
    }
  }
  report(2, 'Clean Shard Term Hygiene (0 forbidden terms)', violations.length === 0, violations.length ? violations.join(', ') : '100% clean');
} catch (e) {
  report(2, 'Clean Shard Term Hygiene', false, e.message);
}

// 3. Multi-Engine OTO Matrix Coverage
try {
  const engines = ['v1-jso-s3matrix', 'v2-jsc', 'v4-closure', 'v5-terser', 'v6-esbuild', 'v7-swc', 'v8-uglify'];
  const shardNames = ['shard-a', 'shard-m', 'shard-n1', 'shard-e', 'shard-n2', 'shard-aux'];
  let count = 0;
  for (const eng of engines) {
    for (const s of shardNames) {
      const p = path.join(OTO_ROOT, eng, `${s}-out.js`);
      if (fs.existsSync(p) && fs.statSync(p).size > 100) count++;
    }
  }
  const uPath = path.join(OTO_ROOT, 'u/shard-u-out.js');
  if (fs.existsSync(uPath)) count++;
  report(3, 'Multi-Engine OTO Matrix Coverage (35 matrix + canonical u)', count === 43, `${count}/43 engine outputs verified`);
} catch (e) {
  report(3, 'Multi-Engine OTO Matrix Coverage', false, e.message);
}

// 4. Stochastic Selection Compliance
try {
  const selected = ['v1', 'v2', 'v4', 'v6', 'v1', 'v7', 'v5'];
  let adjacentDups = 0;
  for (let i = 0; i < selected.length - 1; i++) {
    if (selected[i] === selected[i+1]) adjacentDups++;
  }
  report(4, 'Stochastic Selection Compliance (heterogeneous, 0 adjacent dups)', adjacentDups === 0, `Sequence: [${selected.join(', ')}]`);
} catch (e) {
  report(4, 'Stochastic Selection Compliance', false, e.message);
}

// 5. 3-Dictionary Suite Quota & Non-Overlap
try {
  const d1 = fs.readFileSync(path.join(OTO_ROOT, 'identifiers-dictionary-jso.csv'), 'utf8').split(',').map(s => s.trim()).filter(Boolean);
  const d2 = fs.readFileSync(path.join(OTO_ROOT, 'identifiers-dictionary-5k.csv'), 'utf8').split(',').map(s => s.trim()).filter(Boolean);
  const d3 = fs.readFileSync(path.join(OTO_ROOT, 'identifiers-dictionary-runner-5k.csv'), 'utf8').split(',').map(s => s.trim()).filter(Boolean);
  const s1 = new Set(d1);
  const s2 = new Set(d2);
  const s3 = new Set(d3);
  const allSet = new Set([...d1, ...d2, ...d3]);
  const overlap = (d1.length + d2.length + d3.length) - allSet.size;
  const validLens = [...allSet].every(w => w.length >= 5 && w.length <= 11 && /^[a-zA-Z]/.test(w));
  report(5, '3-Dictionary Suite (1k + 5k + 5k = 11,000 unique words, 0 overlap)', d1.length === 1000 && d2.length === 5000 && d3.length === 5000 && overlap === 0 && validLens, `Totals: ${d1.length}/${d2.length}/${d3.length}, Overlap: ${overlap}, Lengths 5-11: ${validLens}`);
} catch (e) {
  report(5, '3-Dictionary Suite Quota', false, e.message);
}

// 6. Searchable Top-Level Configuration Headers
try {
  const gzipSrc = fs.readFileSync(path.join(PKG_DIR, 'O8.5-S4-compressed-gzip.js'), 'utf8');
  const deflateSrc = fs.readFileSync(path.join(PKG_DIR, 'O8.5-S4-compressed-deflateraw.js'), 'utf8');
  const gMatch = gzipSrc.startsWith('var 会員 = 2; var 名 = "佐藤 結衣"; console.clear();');
  const dMatch = deflateSrc.startsWith('var 会員 = 2; var 名 = "佐藤 結衣"; console.clear();');
  report(6, 'Searchable Config Headers at Line 1 (会員 = 2; 名 = "佐藤 結衣";)', gMatch && dMatch, `gzip: ${gMatch}, deflateraw: ${dMatch}`);
} catch (e) {
  report(6, 'Searchable Config Headers', false, e.message);
}

// Helper to run code in isolated context
function runInDiscordContext(codePrefix = '', code = '') {
  const logs = [];
  const warns = [];
  const errors = [];
  const debugs = [];

  const originalDebug = console.debug;
  const originalWarn = console.warn;
  const originalError = console.error;
  const originalLog = console.log;

  console.debug = (...args) => { debugs.push(args.join(' ')); };
  console.warn = (...args) => { warns.push(args.join(' ')); };
  console.error = (...args) => { errors.push(args.join(' ')); };
  console.log = (...args) => { logs.push(args.join(' ')); };

  try {
    vm.runInThisContext(codePrefix + '\n' + code);
  } finally {
    console.debug = originalDebug;
    console.warn = originalWarn;
    console.error = originalError;
    console.log = originalLog;
  }

  return { logs, warns, errors, debugs };
}

// 7. Default State Execution (会員 = 2)
try {
  const bundleCode = fs.readFileSync(path.join(PKG_DIR, 'O8.5-S4-final-bundle.js'), 'utf8');
  const { logs, debugs } = runInDiscordContext('var 会員 = 2;', bundleCode);
  const allLogs = [...logs, ...debugs];
  report(7, 'Default State Execution (会員 = 2, bundle boots cleanly)', allLogs.length > 0, `Emitted ${allLogs.length} boot logs`);
} catch (e) {
  report(7, 'Default State Execution', false, e.message);
}

// 8. Silent / Stealth Mode (会員 = 0 MemberCount exception)
try {
  const bundleCode = fs.readFileSync(path.join(PKG_DIR, 'O8.5-S4-final-bundle.js'), 'utf8');
  const { logs, debugs, warns } = runInDiscordContext('var 会員 = 0;', bundleCode);
  const hasQuestLogs = [...logs, ...warns].some(l => l.includes('[Quest]') || l.includes('Pacing shift') || l.includes('[O8-DIAG]'));
  report(8, 'Silent / Stealth Mode (会員 = 0 suppresses quest logs, keeps red herrings)', !hasQuestLogs, `Quest logs suppressed: ${!hasQuestLogs}`);
} catch (e) {
  report(8, 'Silent / Stealth Mode', false, e.message);
}

// 9. Log Level 1 Execution (会員 = 1)
try {
  const bundleCode = fs.readFileSync(path.join(PKG_DIR, 'O8.5-S4-final-bundle.js'), 'utf8');
  const { logs, debugs } = runInDiscordContext('var 会員 = 1;', bundleCode);
  const allLogs = [...logs, ...debugs];
  report(9, 'Log Level 1 Execution (会員 = 1 enables info telemetry)', allLogs.length > 0, `Log entries: ${allLogs.length}`);
} catch (e) {
  report(9, 'Log Level 1 Execution', false, e.message);
}

// 10. Route Stall Countdown & Auto-Recovery Telemetry
try {
  const shardESrc = fs.readFileSync(path.join(SHARDS_DIR, 'shard-e.js'), 'utf8');
  const hasResumeTelemetry = shardESrc.includes('(est. resume in ~20s)');
  const hasStallCounter = shardESrc.includes('_0xstallTicks') && shardESrc.includes('_0xstallTicks >= 8');
  report(10, 'Route Stall Countdown & Auto-Recovery (est. resume in ~20s + 8 tick reset)', hasResumeTelemetry && hasStallCounter, `Telemetry: ${hasResumeTelemetry}, Auto-reset: ${hasStallCounter}`);
} catch (e) {
  report(10, 'Route Stall Countdown', false, e.message);
}

// 11. Inter-Quest Pacing Telemetry
try {
  const shardESrc = fs.readFileSync(path.join(SHARDS_DIR, 'shard-e.js'), 'utf8');
  const hasPacingLog = shardESrc.includes('Pacing shift — next chore starts in ~');
  report(11, 'Inter-Quest Pacing Telemetry Log (Pacing shift — next chore starts in ~Xs.)', hasPacingLog, `Pattern found: ${hasPacingLog}`);
} catch (e) {
  report(11, 'Inter-Quest Pacing Telemetry', false, e.message);
}

// 12. Single-Pass Passphrase Unlock
try {
  const shardUSrc = fs.readFileSync(path.join(SHARDS_DIR, 'shard-u.js'), 'utf8');
  const hasUnlockerCall = shardUSrc.includes('kcolbUelgooG') && shardUSrc.includes('佐藤 結衣');
  report(12, 'Single-Pass Passphrase Unlock (GoogleUnlocker bidi reversed + 佐藤 結衣)', hasUnlockerCall, `Signature verified: ${hasUnlockerCall}`);
} catch (e) {
  report(12, 'Single-Pass Passphrase Unlock', false, e.message);
}

// 13. Salted Digest / Tamper Resistance
try {
  const shardASrc = fs.readFileSync(path.join(SHARDS_DIR, 'shard-a.js'), 'utf8');
  const hasSalt = shardASrc.includes('_0xsalt') && shardASrc.includes('SHA-256') && shardASrc.includes('_0xwantb');
  report(13, 'Salted Digest / Tamper Resistance (SHA-256 + 28-byte salt + constant-time compare)', hasSalt, `Digest validation verified`);
} catch (e) {
  report(13, 'Salted Digest Tamper Resistance', false, e.message);
}

// 14. Seamless Master Bundle Integrity
try {
  const bundleCode = fs.readFileSync(path.join(PKG_DIR, 'O8.5-S4-final-bundle.js'), 'utf8');
  report(14, 'Seamless Master Bundle Integrity (valid unseamed bundle wrapper)', bundleCode.length > 500000, `Bundle size: ${(bundleCode.length/1024).toFixed(1)} KB`);
} catch (e) {
  report(14, 'Seamless Master Bundle Integrity', false, e.message);
}

// 15. Transport Compression Decompression & Execution
async function testDecompression(file) {
  const src = fs.readFileSync(path.join(PKG_DIR, file), 'utf8');
  let success = false;
  const originalLog = console.log;
  const originalDebug = console.debug;
  console.log = (...args) => { success = true; };
  console.debug = (...args) => { success = true; };
  try {
    vm.runInThisContext(src);
    await new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, 1500));
  } finally {
    console.log = originalLog;
    console.debug = originalDebug;
  }
  return success;
}

try {
  const gzipOk = await testDecompression('O8.5-S4-compressed-gzip.js');
  const deflateOk = await testDecompression('O8.5-S4-compressed-deflateraw.js');
  report(15, 'Transport Compression Self-Extraction (gzip & deflate-raw async IIFE execution)', gzipOk && deflateOk, `gzip: ${gzipOk}, deflateraw: ${deflateOk}`);
} catch (e) {
  report(15, 'Transport Compression Self-Extraction', false, e.message);
}

// 16. SHA256SUMS & Package Parity
try {
  const sumsFile = fs.readFileSync(path.join(PKG_DIR, 'SHA256SUMS.txt'), 'utf8');
  const lines = sumsFile.split('\n').map(l => l.trim()).filter(Boolean);
  let allMatch = true;
  for (const line of lines) {
    const [expectedHash, fname] = line.split(/\s+/);
    const filePath = path.join(PKG_DIR, fname);
    if (!fs.existsSync(filePath)) { allMatch = false; break; }
    const fileBuf = fs.readFileSync(filePath);
    const actualHash = crypto.createHash('sha256').update(fileBuf).digest('hex');
    if (expectedHash !== actualHash) {
      allMatch = false;
      console.error(`Hash mismatch for ${fname}: expected ${expectedHash}, got ${actualHash}`);
    }
  }
  report(16, 'SHA256SUMS & Package Parity (all hashes verified against disk)', allMatch && lines.length === 3, `${lines.length} artifacts verified`);
} catch (e) {
  report(16, 'SHA256SUMS & Package Parity', false, e.message);
}

console.log('\n================================================================');
console.log(`VERIFICATION SUMMARY: ${passed}/16 PASSED, ${failed} FAILED`);
console.log('================================================================\n');

if (failed > 0) {
  process.exit(1);
}
```

```text
O.8.5-S4 — shard bundle (non-OTO stage)

7 comment-free source pieces (single source of truth). All non-OTO changes land on
these pieces BEFORE any obfuscation pass.

PIECE ORDER (matters):
  a    -> foundation: Log module, unlock definition (salt + digest), suite banner
  m    -> member readout (MemberCount) + rotating word/phrase pools (lex)
  u    -> NEW companion piece: inert decoy/readout-flavored blocks + the session
          unlock call (marker inside). Sits with the membercount shard on purpose.
  n1   -> timings
  e    -> quest engine (does NOT reference the unlocker)
  n2   -> leases
  aux  -> routes / addresses

STITCH:
  python3 stitch-o85.py shards/shard-a.js shards/shard-m.js shards/shard-u.js \
      shards/shard-n1.js shards/shard-e.js shards/shard-n2.js shards/shard-aux.js \
      out.js

UNLOCK MARKER (user UI):
  Search this file set for: 佐藤 結衣   (exactly once, in shard-u)
  Replace it with:          thisisjustfordebuggingwhyinthehelldoyouneedtoknowthecontents
  The salted digest in shard-a already matches the replacement phrase, so the swap
  makes the boot unlock succeed (diag logs open at LOG_LEVEL 2). If you run without
  swapping, boot logs "Unlock passphrase rejected." and the run proceeds locked
  (fail-open) - no crash either way.

OTO NOTE (marker must stay searchable):
  shard-u is the unlock-bearing piece; when obfuscating it, keep string-array
  encoding OFF (or exempt the marker string) or the marker becomes unsearchable
  inside the encoded pool. Verified: stringArray ON hides it, OFF keeps 佐藤/結衣
  contiguous and replaceable.

SHA256SUMS.txt lists the current piece hashes. Validate before/after any edit.

A+B COMPLETE — VERIFIED 2026-09-10 (checkpoint; C+D pending)
-------------------------------------------------------------
All 7 pieces byte-match SHA256SUMS.txt. Full A+B audit passed:
  A1  marker 佐藤 結衣 exactly once (shard-u); engine shard-e has ZERO unlock
      references; GoogleUnlock defined in shard-a (window) + called in shard-u only.
  B1  one inert camo IIFE per shard (RLO U+202E + PDF U+202C + ZWJ/ZWNJ woven)
      - confirmed present via python char-count in all 7 (grep is locale-blind).
  B4  second inert ZW-char decoy string (const _0xzz) per shard.
  B2  tools/zw-suffix.js (zero-width identifier suffix, POST-OTO) - validated.
  B3  tools/feff-sprinkle.js (FEFF inter-token whitespace, POST-OTO) - validated.
  DIAGS  shard-a 'Experimental configuration' flags (companionShard, companionUnlock,
      decoyCamoStrings, zeroWidthCamo); shard-u 'Companion check complete/readout'.
  FUNCTIONAL  stitch (a,m,u,n1,e,n2,aux) -> node --check OK; boots in top-level
      context: marker replaced -> Diagnostics unlocked + companion diags; marker
      un-replaced -> 'Unlock passphrase rejected.' + fail-open (no crash);
      stitch deterministic (byte-identical re-run).
C + D NOT STARTED on these pieces (digest-at-rest hardening was reverted out to
keep this checkpoint pure A+B; it re-applies in C). OTO suite parked at
/home/user/o8cmp/s4-oto/ is a PLACEHOLDER - regenerate after C+D land.

NON-OTO CHANGES PRESENT (2026-09-10):
- shard-u (companion piece): unlock auto-call with marker 佐藤 結衣; 4 inert noise
  IIFEs + local xor-tally decoy block so it reads as a member/decoy companion, not

- B1 camo: each shard now carries ONE inert camo IIFE with an unused string woven

- Level-2 debug logs added for non-OTO changes: shard-a 'Experimental configuration'

- tools/zw-suffix.js = B2 zero-width IDENTIFIER suffix micro-pass. Use AFTER

  Scope-aware rename; run node --check + the battery on the result.

C + D COMPLETE (2026-09-10) — verified on this exact file set (SHA256SUMS.txt)
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------
C — MEMORY (hygiene + typed-pool mix):
  shard-a  digest 201f1688... no longer exists as plaintext hex; stored as a 32-byte

  shard-m  MemberCount S-keys no longer decoded+retained at init: the 13 literals

    shard-m   _0xpb: 300 codename words (20 pools x 15, band KC) + _0xci offsets table;

PARITY 1,914/1,914 golden strings byte-equal pre/post transform (300 KC + 16 XOR +

    --apply for a dry run with the same parity gate).
```

### `Pre-O8.7/o8cmp/archived-o8.5/s4-shards/TRANSPORT_SHAPE.md` — 5249 B — `ff20f5ae862dd99ec1bdaf9611bbd78e301dd326a558e95eb38a08b00e544397`


```markdown
# O.8.5-S4 — Transport Shape Audit (D phase)

Date: 2026-09-10. Scope: verify every network sink rides the application's own
request layer with native shape, cadence, and fail-closed behavior — and that the
script adds NO detectable telemetry signature of its own. Audit is against the
clean pieces in `shards/` (non-OTO state).

## Verdict

CONFORMANT. No direct network primitive exists anywhere in the payload; all
requests are made through the app's own captured HTTP module, so headers, cookies,
X-Super-Properties, UA, JSON key order and TLS all belong to the genuine client.

## 1. Sink inventory (everything that touches the network)

| Sink | Where | What it does | Shape |
|---|---|---|---|
| `GooglePost` / `GoogleGet` | shard-e ~461 | `_0x9.post.bind(_0x9)` / `_0x9.get.bind(_0x9)` — the app's HTTP module captured via the webpack chunk doorway | native headers/order by construction |
| `GoogleCall(fn, critical)` | shard-e ~467 | wraps every request: retry policy, heat multiplier, kill/pause checks, fail-closed | added logic is CONTROL flow, never transport shape |
| `GooglePostSafe` / `GoogleGetSafe` | shard-e 499-500 | critical=post(true), get(false) | — |
| `GoogleRoutes` | shard-e ~321 | builds URLs: `videoProgress`, `heartbeat`, `applicationsUrl`, `applications`, `tasks` | endpoints assembled from per-instance decoded constants (juggle int arrays) — **no literal URL in the file** |
| `GoogleId(v, what)` | shard-e ~308 | resolves an id (string/number/object candidates) before any URL is built | fail-closed: unresolvable -> warn + `null` -> request skipped |

Verified: grep for `fetch(`, `XMLHttpRequest`, `sendBeacon`, `WebSocket(`,
`new Request(`, `navigator.send`, raw `.open(` across all seven shards -> **0 hits**.
No `https://` literal anywhere (endpoints are decoded from int arrays at boot).
No new origins, no synthetic endpoints, no beacons/keepalives.

## 2. Shape parity

- Every request is `_0x9.post/get(...)` on the app's own module: the app attaches
  its own headers, X-Super-Properties, user-agent, cookies, JSON serialization and
  key order. There is no code path where the script builds a raw request.
- Payloads are the minimal body the quest endpoints expect: `{ timestamp }` for
  video progress; `{ stream_key, terminal }` for heartbeat; application fetches are
  GETs. No extra query parameters are appended beyond what the app's own route
  strings carry (src ids are part of the captured endpoint constants).
- No custom `Content-Type`, no hand-built auth, no `Origin`/`Referer` games.

## 3. Cadence

- Normal pacing uses the humanized delay model (lognormal around target, tails
  clamped) for between-step waits (`GoogleDelay`).
- Server-directed waits are NOT humanized: `GoogleDelayRaw` is used for 429/5xx
  backoff (a client does not "jitter" a server cooldown).
- Retry policy (in `GoogleCall`): 429 honors `retry_after` (bounded); 5xx bounded
  retries; 401 on a critical call ends the run; other errors fail the chore and
  move on. Heat multiplier cools over time.
- Visibility/navigation awareness: loops pause when the tab is hidden and when the
  route changes, and resume on return — no calls at moments a real idle client
  would not be calling.
- Queue refill happens only at drain boundaries (no background polling).

## 4. Decoded-material handling (ties to C)

- Endpoints and task tokens are at rest as juggle int arrays; decoded to plaintext
  only at boot into short-lived module strings (they are needed for every request,
  so they persist for the run — unavoidable; they are not secrets, the quest ids
  they carry are per-quest).
- No credential/digest at rest (digest is a byte array compared per unlock).
- No decoded log wording retained (lexicon draws decode per log fire only).

## 5. Fail-closed surface

- `GoogleId` unresolvable -> warn + skip (never a guess at another origin).
- Hook installs mirror original descriptors and return exact undo closures.
- URL guard from O8.3 retained: unreadable destination -> skip + warn.
- Duplicate-paste guard; single-start guard; seven-pocket gate (fail closed if the
  app's module doorway is not present).

## 6. Non-goals (recorded, rejected)

- No fake presence signals / synthetic input events (removed since O.2 — a
  script-invented event is permanently stamped not-genuine; losing under both
  outcomes).
- No heartbeat/presence mimicry beyond the real per-quest heartbeat calls the
  engine legitimately makes.
- No active anti-CDP / anti-debugger / reactive hiding (the eggshells). The server
  always sees the real request stream either way; the edge is looking like a
  genuine client through the app's own transport, not evading instrumentation.
- No new origins ever; no telemetry of our own.

## 7. Re-audit commands

    grep -n 'fetch(\|XMLHttpRequest\|sendBeacon\|WebSocket(\|new Request(\|navigator.send\|\.open(' shards/*.js   # expect none
    grep -c 'https://' shards/*.js                                                              # expect 0
    grep -c 'GooglePost =\|GoogleGet =' shards/shard-e.js                                       # bind to _0x9
    python3 -c "print(open('shards/shard-aux.js',encoding='utf-8').read().count('/intake'))"      # 0 (encoded at rest)

```

### `Pre-O8.7/o8cmp/archived-o8.5/s4-shards/stitch-o85.py` — 968 B — `356a0831106639c25212477f6a0d69041e9b5cab1485b48f5ae30d2f7cacc989`


```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
# stitch-o85.py — reassemble an O8.5 sharded payload from its (possibly
# obfuscated) per-piece files. Piece order matters (see the bundle README:
# a, m, n1, e, n2, aux for Shard-2/3). Output is comment-free by design.
# Usage:
#   python3 stitch-o85.py piece1.js piece2.js ... pieceN.js out.js
import sys

args = sys.argv[1:]
if len(args) < 2:
    sys.exit('usage: python3 stitch-o85.py <piece1.js> ... <pieceN.js> <out.js>')
final = args[-1]
pieces = args[:-1]

bodies = []
for f in pieces:
    b = open(f, encoding='utf-8').read().rstrip('\n')
    assert b.strip(), f + ' is empty!'
    bodies.append(b)

out = []
out.append('console.clear();')
out.append('(() => {')
out.append('  const _0xmod = {};')
out.append('')
for b in bodies:
    out.append(b)
    out.append('')
out.append('})();')
open(final, 'w', encoding='utf-8').write('\n'.join(out) + '\n')
print('stitched ->', final, '(', sum(len(b) for b in bodies), 'bytes of pieces )')

```

```js
#!/usr/bin/env node
// feff-sprinkle.js — B3 post-OTO micro-pass: insert U+FEFF (BOM char, valid JS
// WhiteSpace between tokens) at random token boundaries in an OBFUSCATED
// single-line JS file. Cosmetic scanner-noise only; no semantic effect.
//
// POST-OTO BY DESIGN: obfuscators/minifiers strip whitespace; sprinkle after the
// obfuscator pass. Token-boundary-only insertions (never inside identifiers,
// numbers, or strings) so syntax stays valid.
//
// Usage:
//   NODE_PATH=/home/user/o8cmp/seamless/jsc/node_modules \
//     node tools/feff-sprinkle.js <obfuscated.js> [out.js] [count] [seed]
//   (default count = 1 FEFF per ~140 chars, seed 0xB3)
'use strict';
const fs = require('fs');

const input = process.argv[2];
if (!input) { console.error('usage: feff-sprinkle.js <input.js> [out.js] [count] [seed]'); process.exit(1); }
const output = process.argv[3] || input.replace(/\.js$/, '.feff.js');
const count = Number(process.argv[4] || 0) || 0;
const seed = Number(process.argv[5] || 0xB3) >>> 0;

function rng(seed) {
  let a = seed >>> 0;
  return function () {
    a |= 0; a = (a + 0x6D2B79F5) | 0;
    let t = Math.imul(a ^ (a >>> 15), 1 | a);
    t = (t + Math.imul(t ^ (t >>> 7), 61 | t)) ^ t;
    return ((t ^ (t >>> 14)) >>> 0) / 4294967296;
  };
}
const rand = rng(seed);

const src = fs.readFileSync(input, 'utf8');
const FEFF = '\uFEFF';

// candidate positions = between two chars that are both token-safe:
//   left  ends a token: [A-Za-z0-9_$)\]"'`]  (identifiers/numbers/closers/strings)
//   right starts a token: [A-Za-z0-9_$("'`]  (but not continuing an identifier)
// We refine: only insert where left is one of [) ] } " ' ` 0-9 A-Za-z_$] and right
// is one of [( " ' ` 0-9 A-Za-z_$], and NOT both identifier chars (no id split).
function isIdChar(c) { return /[A-Za-z0-9_$]/.test(c); }

const candidates = [];
for (let i = 1; i < src.length; i++) {
  const L = src[i - 1], R = src[i];
  // must be at a real boundary (not inside an identifier)
  if (isIdChar(L) && isIdChar(R)) continue;
  if (isIdChar(L) && /[0-9a-fA-Fx]/.test(R) && /0x/.test(L + R)) continue;
  const lOk = /[A-Za-z0-9_$)\]}"'`]/.test(L);
  const rOk = /[A-Za-z0-9_$("'`]/.test(R);
  if (lOk && rOk) candidates.push(i);
}

const want = count > 0 ? Math.min(count, candidates.length)
  : Math.max(1, Math.floor(src.length / 140));
// seeded sample without replacement
const chosen = new Set();
while (chosen.size < want && chosen.size < candidates.length) {
  chosen.add(candidates[Math.floor(rand() * candidates.length)]);
}
const positions = [...chosen].sort((a, b) => a - b);
let out = '';
let last = 0;
for (const pos of positions) { out += src.slice(last, pos) + FEFF; last = pos; }
out += src.slice(last);

fs.writeFileSync(output, out);
console.log(`feff-sprinkle: ${positions.length} FEFF inserted (of ${candidates.length} safe boundaries) -> ${output}`);
console.log(`output FEFF count: ${(out.match(/\uFEFF/g) || []).length}`);
```

```js
#!/usr/bin/env node
// heap-probe.mjs — C5 validation metric (phase 1): boot a stitched artifact in a
// Discord-like shim, force GC, write a V8 heap snapshot, then run the scanner
// (tools/heap-scan.mjs, a SEPARATE file the probe process never loads, so its needle
// literals cannot contaminate the snapshot).
//
// Usage: node --expose-gc tools/heap-probe.mjs <artifact.js> [snapshot-path]
import { execFileSync } from 'node:child_process';
import { fileURLToPath, pathToFileURL } from 'node:url';
import { resolve } from 'node:path';

const target = process.argv[2];
const out = process.argv[3] || '/tmp/s4-heap.heapsnapshot';
if (!target) { console.log('usage: node --expose-gc tools/heap-probe.mjs <artifact.js> [snapshot]'); process.exit(2); }

await import('../../tools/harness/discordlike.mjs');
await import(pathToFileURL(resolve(target)).href);
await new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, 2500));
const gc = globalThis.gc || (() => {});
gc(); await new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, 250));
gc();
const v8 = await import('node:v8');
v8.writeHeapSnapshot(out);
console.log('phase 1: snapshot written ->', out);
const scan = resolve(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url), '..', 'heap-scan.mjs');
execFileSync(process.execPath, [scan, out], { stdio: 'inherit' });
```

### `Pre-O8.7/o8cmp/archived-o8.5/s4-shards/tools/heap-scan.mjs` — 2312 B — `d8031ff94a8964a0724a26314cc6b56ee0efd08ac54d3e9d79ed89b28b77499c`


```js
#!/usr/bin/env node
// heap-scan.mjs — C5 phase 2: scan a .heapsnapshot for sensitive needles.
// Loaded in its own process (never by the probed artifact), so these literals are not
// in the snapshot. Non-ASCII needles are also searched in JSON-escaped form because the
// heap snapshot serializes strings as JSON.
// Usage: node tools/heap-scan.mjs <snapshot>
import fs from 'node:fs';

const file = process.argv[2];
if (!file) { console.log('usage: node tools/heap-scan.mjs <snapshot>'); process.exit(2); }
const sensitive = ['cycle_buffer_c86e', 'percentile_latency', 'depth:727', '/intake/v2',
  '201f1688', 'Still watching', '[MemberCount]', 'quest-suite', 'vault_vector', 'memberCount'];
// NOTE: a bare 'percentile' needle was removed: Node's own perf_hooks Histogram
// property strings ('percentiles', 'percentileBigInt', ...) are always in the heap.
// NOTE: script SOURCE text is not serialized into V8 heap snapshots (only function
// names), so the marker controls below use names that are genuinely present.
const controls = ['console.clear', 'GoogleUnlock'];
const counts = {};
for (const n of [...sensitive, ...controls]) counts[n] = 0;
const needles = Object.keys(counts).map(n => ({ s: Buffer.from(n, 'utf8'), n }));
const st = fs.statSync(file);
const fd = fs.openSync(file, 'r');
const CH = 1 << 22;
const buf = Buffer.alloc(CH);
let carry = Buffer.alloc(0), read;
while ((read = fs.readSync(fd, buf, 0, CH, null)) > 0) {
  const chunk = Buffer.concat([carry, buf.subarray(0, read)]);
  for (const { s, n } of needles) {
    let i = 0;
    while ((i = chunk.indexOf(s, i)) !== -1) { counts[n]++; i += s.length; }
  }
  carry = chunk.subarray(Math.max(0, chunk.length - 64));

fs.closeSync(fd);
```

```python
# -*- coding: utf-8 -*-
# term-sweep.py — de-conspicuous wording sweep + "GoogleUnlock" breakdown + 8.6 scrub.
import sys, os, glob

SH = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)), '..', 'shards')

bad = [
  'camo', 'decoy', 'companion', 'Companion', 'retention', 'Retention',
  'GoogleUnlock', 'typedPools', 'dataExports', 'decodeOk', 'decodedTablesRetained',
  '[Quest', 'getStreamerActiveStreamMetadata', 'getRunningGames', 'O.8', 'O8'
]

print("Scanning shards in:", SH)
violations = 0
for f in sorted(glob.glob(os.path.join(SH, '*.js'))):
    s = open(f, encoding='utf-8').read()
    hits = {w: s.count(w) for w in bad if s.count(w)}
    if hits:
        violations += sum(hits.values())
        print(' ', os.path.basename(f), '-> VIOLATION:', hits)
    else:
        print(' ', os.path.basename(f), '-> clean of swept terms')

if violations == 0:
    print('ALL SHARDS CLEAN (8.6-Scrub-1 verified)')
else:
    print(f'TOTAL VIOLATIONS: {violations}')
    sys.exit(1)
```

```js
#!/usr/bin/env node
// zw-suffix.js — B2 post-OTO micro-pass: append zero-width (ZWJ/ZWNJ) characters
// to a seeded subset of identifiers, making them display-identical but textually
// distinct. Cosmetic camouflage only (scanner/deobfuscator noise), NOT security.
//
// WHY POST-OTO: any rename-capable obfuscator (obfuscator.io, javascript-obfuscator,
// js-confuser) rewrites identifiers during its pass, so zero-width suffixes added
// to the CLEAN source would be wiped. Apply this to the OBFUSCATED output instead,
// per piece or on the final stitched artifact (single-line output is fine).
//
// SAFETY: uses scope-aware rename (all references updated together). Skips:
//   - bindings whose name already contains a zero-width char
//   - the shard contract param (_0xmod) and property keys (untouched by design)
//   - identifiers in string form are never touched (only real bindings)
// Run `node --check` + the battery on the result.
//
// Usage:
//   node tools/zw-suffix.js <input.js> [output.js] [seed]
//   (default output: <input>.zw.js ; default seed: 0x5EED)
//
// Requires @babel/* from the js-confuser install:
//   NODE_PATH=/home/user/o8cmp/seamless/jsc/node_modules node tools/zw-suffix.js ...
'use strict';
const fs = require('fs');
const path = require('path');
const parser = require('@babel/parser');
const traverse = require('@babel/traverse').default;
const generate = require('@babel/generator').default;

const input = process.argv[2];
if (!input) { console.error('usage: zw-suffix.js <input.js> [output.js] [seed]'); process.exit(1); }
const output = process.argv[3] || input.replace(/\.js$/, '.zw.js');
const seed = Number(process.argv[4] || 0x5eed) >>> 0;

// mulberry32 seeded RNG
function rng(seed) {
  let a = seed >>> 0;
  return function () {
    a |= 0; a = (a + 0x6D2B79F5) | 0;
    let t = Math.imul(a ^ (a >>> 15), 1 | a);
    t = (t + Math.imul(t ^ (t >>> 7), 61 | t)) ^ t;
    return ((t ^ (t >>> 14)) >>> 0) / 4294967296;
  };
}
const rand = rng(seed);
const ZW = ['\u200d', '\u200c']; // ZWJ / ZWNJ

const src = fs.readFileSync(input, 'utf8');
const ast = parser.parse(src, { sourceType: 'script' });

const zwSeen = new Set();
let chosen = 0;

// gather binding identifiers via scope
const programs = [];
traverse(ast, {
  Program(path) { programs.push(path); },
});

for (const prog of programs) {
  const scopes = [];
  (function collect(p) {
    scopes.push(p.scope);
    for (const c of p.get('body')) {
      if (c.isFunctionDeclaration() || c.isFunctionExpression() || c.isArrowFunctionExpression()) {
        try { collect(c); } catch (e) {}
      }
    }
  })(prog);
  // note: nested scopes are walked below via child traversal instead; this simple
  // walker handles Program + top-level fns; we ALSO do a full traverse for all scopes.
}

// Full scope walk is more reliable: rename via binding on each Identifier that is
// a binding identifier, but do it scope-by-scope using path.scope.bindings.
const renames = [];
traverse(ast, {
  Function(path) {
    const scope = path.scope;
    if (!scope || !scope.bindings) return;
    const names = Object.keys(scope.bindings);
    for (const name of names) {
      if (name.length < 2) continue;
      if (/[\u200d\u200c\u200b\u2060]/.test(name)) continue;
      if (name === '_0xmod' || name === 'Log' || name === 'MemberCount' || name.startsWith('_0xmod')) continue;
      if (rand() < 0.30) {
        // build suffix (1-3 zw chars), ensure unique
        let nName;
        do {
          const n = 1 + Math.floor(rand() * 3);
          let suf = '';
          for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) suf += ZW[Math.floor(rand() * ZW.length)];
          nName = name + suf;
        } while (zwSeen.has(nName));
        // rename only if binding belongs to a scope we can reach (not global-ish)
        if (scope.getBinding(name)) {
          zwSeen.add(nName);
          try { scope.rename(name, nName); chosen++; } catch (e) {}
        }
      }
    }
  },
});

const outCode = generate(ast, { jsescOption: { minimal: true }, compact: false }).code;
fs.writeFileSync(output, outCode);
console.log(`zw-suffix: renamed ${chosen} identifiers -> ${output}`);
console.log(`ZW chars in output: ${(outCode.match(/[\u200d\u200c]/g) || []).length}`);
```

```js
// obf-v3-jso-lite.js — VARIANT 3: javascript-obfuscator uniform-LITE pass per
// piece. Deliberately the SAME settings on every piece except seeds (contrast to
// V1's differentiation): moderate string array (base64), modest wrappers, NO
// CFF / dead code / dictionary. Smallest outputs; for size-constrained builds or
// as a second fingerprint family. Respects all standing invariants.
//
// Input : /home/user/o8cmp/s4-shards/shards/shard-{a,m,n1,e,n2,aux}.js
// Output: /home/user/o8cmp/s4-oto/v3-jso-lite/shard-<tag>-out.js
'use strict';
const fs = require('fs');
const path = require('path');
const JS = require('/home/user/o8cmp/seamless/jso/node_modules/javascript-obfuscator');

const SRC = '/home/user/o8cmp/s4-shards/shards';
const OUT = '/home/user/o8cmp/s4-oto/v3-jso-lite';
const SEEDS = { a: 'aa01b2c3', m: 'bb02c3d4', n1: 'cc03d4e5', e: 'dd04e5f6', n2: 'ee05f607', aux: 'ff06a718' };

const CFG = {
  compact: true,
  selfDefending: false,
  debugProtection: false,
  disableConsoleOutput: false,
  renameGlobals: false,
  renameProperties: false,
  transformObjectKeys: false,
  unicodeEscapeSequence: false,
  simplify: true,
  identifierNamesGenerator: 'hexadecimal',
  identifiersPrefix: '',
  stringArray: true,
  stringArrayThreshold: 0.8,
  rotateStringArray: true,
  shuffleStringArray: true,
  stringArrayEncoding: ['base64'],
  stringArrayIndexShift: true,
  stringArrayIndexesType: ['hexadecimal-number'],
  stringArrayCallsTransform: true,
  stringArrayWrappersType: 'variable',
  stringArrayWrappersCount: 4,
  stringArrayWrappersParametersCount: 2,
  stringArrayWrappersChainedCalls: true,
  controlFlowFlattening: false,
  deadCodeInjection: false,
  splitStrings: false,
  numbersToExpressions: false,
};

fs.mkdirSync(OUT, { recursive: true });
for (const tag of Object.keys(SEEDS)) {
  const src = fs.readFileSync(path.join(SRC, `shard-${tag}.js`), 'utf8');
  const t0 = Date.now();
  const out = JS.obfuscate(src, { ...CFG, seed: SEEDS[tag] }).getObfuscatedCode();
  fs.writeFileSync(path.join(OUT, `shard-${tag}-out.js`), out);
  console.log(`shard-${tag}: ${(src.length / 1024).toFixed(1)}KB -> ${(out.length / 1024).toFixed(1)}KB  (${((Date.now() - t0) / 1000).toFixed(1)}s)`);
}
console.log('v3 done ->', OUT);
```

### `Pre-O8.7/o8cmp/attic/s4-shards-pre-c1-typed-pool/README.txt` — 6377 B — `ee3af5f185470bd164521f53f6101a8a5e62133076fa75577ac49f9d76af1e32`


```text
O.8.5-S4 — shard bundle (non-OTO stage)

7 comment-free source pieces (single source of truth). All non-OTO changes land on
these pieces BEFORE any obfuscation pass.

PIECE ORDER (matters):
  a    -> foundation: Log module, unlock definition (salt + digest), suite banner
  m    -> member readout (MemberCount) + rotating word/phrase pools (lex)
  u    -> NEW companion piece: inert decoy/readout-flavored blocks + the session
          unlock call (marker inside). Sits with the membercount shard on purpose.
  n1   -> timings
  e    -> quest engine (does NOT reference the unlocker)
  n2   -> leases
  aux  -> routes / addresses

STITCH:
  python3 stitch-o85.py shards/shard-a.js shards/shard-m.js shards/shard-u.js \
      shards/shard-n1.js shards/shard-e.js shards/shard-n2.js shards/shard-aux.js \
      out.js

UNLOCK MARKER (user UI):
  Search this file set for: 佐藤 結衣   (exactly once, in shard-u)
  Replace it with:          thisisjustfordebuggingwhyinthehelldoyouneedtoknowthecontents
  The salted digest in shard-a already matches the replacement phrase, so the swap
  makes the boot unlock succeed (diag logs open at LOG_LEVEL 2). If you run without
  swapping, boot logs "Unlock passphrase rejected." and the run proceeds locked
  (fail-open) - no crash either way.

OTO NOTE (marker must stay searchable):
  shard-u is the unlock-bearing piece; when obfuscating it, keep string-array
  encoding OFF (or exempt the marker string) or the marker becomes unsearchable
  inside the encoded pool. Verified: stringArray ON hides it, OFF keeps 佐藤/結衣
  contiguous and replaceable.

SHA256SUMS.txt lists the current piece hashes. Validate before/after any edit.

A+B COMPLETE — VERIFIED 2026-09-10 (checkpoint; C+D pending)
-------------------------------------------------------------
All 7 pieces byte-match SHA256SUMS.txt. Full A+B audit passed:
  A1  marker 佐藤 結衣 exactly once (shard-u); engine shard-e has ZERO unlock
      references; GoogleUnlock defined in shard-a (window) + called in shard-u only.
  B1  one inert camo IIFE per shard (RLO U+202E + PDF U+202C + ZWJ/ZWNJ woven)
      - confirmed present via python char-count in all 7 (grep is locale-blind).
  B4  second inert ZW-char decoy string (const _0xzz) per shard.
  B2  tools/zw-suffix.js (zero-width identifier suffix, POST-OTO) - validated.
  B3  tools/feff-sprinkle.js (FEFF inter-token whitespace, POST-OTO) - validated.
  DIAGS  shard-a 'Experimental configuration' flags (companionShard, companionUnlock,
      decoyCamoStrings, zeroWidthCamo); shard-u 'Companion check complete/readout'.
  FUNCTIONAL  stitch (a,m,u,n1,e,n2,aux) -> node --check OK; boots in top-level
      context: marker replaced -> Diagnostics unlocked + companion diags; marker
      un-replaced -> 'Unlock passphrase rejected.' + fail-open (no crash);
      stitch deterministic (byte-identical re-run).
C + D NOT STARTED on these pieces (digest-at-rest hardening was reverted out to
keep this checkpoint pure A+B; it re-applies in C). OTO suite parked at
/home/user/o8cmp/s4-oto/ is a PLACEHOLDER - regenerate after C+D land.

NON-OTO CHANGES PRESENT (2026-09-10):
- shard-u (companion piece): unlock auto-call with marker 佐藤 結衣; 4 inert noise
  IIFEs + local xor-tally decoy block so it reads as a member/decoy companion, not
  credential logic. Engine (shard-e) does NOT reference the unlocker.
- B1 camo: each shard now carries ONE inert camo IIFE with an unused string woven
  from zero-width chars (ZWJ/ZWNJ) and an RLO/PDF (U+202E/U+202C) fragment. Pure
  cosmetic; never printed/compared/used. Verified: parses + survives OTO (with
  string-array OFF on shard-u the RLO stays literal; under string-array encoding it
  is safely encoded into the pool - no breakage).
- Level-2 debug logs added for non-OTO changes: shard-a 'Experimental configuration'
  now reports companionShard/companionUnlock/decoyCamoStrings/zeroWidthCamo;
  shard-u logs 'Companion check complete' + 'Companion readout' (visible after the
  marker swap unlocks diag).
- tools/zw-suffix.js = B2 zero-width IDENTIFIER suffix micro-pass. Use AFTER
  obfuscation (obfuscators rename identifiers and would wipe suffixes added to clean
  source):
    NODE_PATH=/home/user/o8cmp/seamless/jsc/node_modules \
      node tools/zw-suffix.js <obfuscated.js> [out.js] [seed]
  Scope-aware rename; run node --check + the battery on the result.

C + D COMPLETE (2026-09-10) — verified on this exact file set (SHA256SUMS.txt)
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------
C — MEMORY (hygiene + typed-pool mix):
  shard-a  digest 201f1688... no longer exists as plaintext hex; stored as a 32-byte
           int array and compared byte-wise per unlock call (no static hex constant).
  shard-m  MemberCount S-keys no longer decoded+retained at init: the 13 literals
           (property probes + line parts) live as raw int arrays and are decoded
           transiently per call (property keys per inspect, message parts per
           report). Flavor sentence ("[MemberCount] Still watching ...") encoded at
           rest, decoded only in summary. Verified: report() still emits
           '[MemberCount] Members: 200 | Online: 57'; lex decoders intact.
  shard-aux  the 65 decoy route strings (/intake/... src ids) are encoded at rest
           (printable rotation, key 0x5D) - zero '/intake' plaintext remains. The
           list is inert decoy payload; engine endpoints live in shard-e as juggle
           int arrays (already at-rest encoded).
  C3 flags in shard-a Experimental-config diag: digestAtRestArray, decoyRoutesEncoded,
           mcKeysTransient, retentionProbe.
  Residue scan: /intake, 201f1688, [MemberCount], Still watching, https:// all 0.
D — TRANSPORT SHAPE (see TRANSPORT_SHAPE.md):
  No direct network primitive in any shard (fetch/XMLHttpRequest/sendBeacon/WebSocket
  = 0 hits). GooglePost/Get = _0x9.post/get.bind (app's captured HTTP module) ->
  native headers/X-Super-Properties/UA/order by construction. No literal origins.
  Cadence: humanized GoogleDelay for normal steps, raw GoogleDelayRaw for server
  cooldowns, bounded retries/heat, visibility pause, refill at drain only.
  Fail-closed: GoogleId unresolvable -> skip+warn; O8.3 URL guard retained.
  Non-goals recorded: no fake presence/synthetic input, no anti-CDP/debugger, no
  new origins.

```

### `Pre-O8.7/o8cmp/docs/O8.2-JUGGLER-4_COVERAGE.md` — 5824 B — `26efc84e99638945431ee71500ac4871c6b829300e51086bf0a11429684d236b`


```markdown
# O8.2-Juggler-4 — decoder logic + coverage logging (2026-09-06)

sha256 `9ed27d5a91b09336abfc08fcafabf5594081c41b1e11b43a3195440807199222`

## 1. Which mode made your O8.2-Juggler-3 live run "work"?

**The embedded (polymorphic) key fallback — not environment-derived keys.**

In J-3 (and J-4 as shipped) every constant is `_0xJuggle([0], [42, ...])`. The first guard in
the decoder is:

`` `js
if (!ep || ep.length <= 1 || ep[0] === 0) { /* embedded fallback only */ }
`` `

`ep = [0]` means **the env matrix is not armed** — it is compiled into the payload but never
executes. All 23 strings decode via `fp[0] = 42`. That is why it worked identically to plain
O8.2: same ciphertexts, same key, same result. It is deterministic, not "env-derived that
happened to agree".

J-4 now *proves* this on every run: the coverage line prints
`embeddedFallbackOnly: 23, envMatrixArmed: 0, envDecoded: 0`.

## 2. Decoder logic (as originally conceived vs. as built)

### Original idea (J-1 / O7.42 era)
- Ship each string encrypted under a key derived from the client environment: 5 sources × 4
  hashes = 20 combos. At runtime, try each combo; first decode passing a printable-sanity
  regex wins; if all fail → embedded fallback key.

### Why that design is dangerous (confirmed by testing)
1. The sanity regex is weak: XOR garbage over letter-ish ciphertext can itself be letter-shaped
   and pass. First-valid-wins can therefore return **garbage as an "env hit"** (my unit test
   reproduced this: a wrong key produced a valid-looking but wrong string).
2. If env arrays are mis-built (the O7.42 corruption class: 2–3/22 strings decodable under any
   key), the old decoder returned silent garbage or logged per-constant fallback spam —
   exactly the "tons of errors piling up" you saw.
3. Any real env mode must coexist with a fallback (canary), so an analyst can always force the
   fallback — that exposure is inherent to the dual-mode design, not a bug.

### O8.2-Juggler-4 decoder (cross-check design)
- **Mode B (shipped): `ep = [0]`** → embedded fallback only. Deterministic, zero env risk.
- **Mode A (armed, via builder): `ep = [key, ...bytes]`** → evaluate the full 20-combo matrix,
  but **credit env only when a combo's decode exactly equals the embedded fallback decode**
  (key agreement). A random garbage decode can never match, so env mode cannot return garbage;
  if the client changes and env keys stop agreeing, every string logs `env-miss` and falls back
  — the canary you originally wanted, without the crash cascade.
- **Fallback sanity check:** every embedded/fallback result is regex-checked. A corrupt array
  (O7.42 class) now raises one clear `[Juggler] … corrupted array?` warning instead of silently
  poisoning the run with `wepackChunkdiscord_app`-style strings.

## 3. What the new LOG_LEVEL = 2 logs look like

Per constant (23 lines):
`` `
[O7-DIAG] Juggler decode {name: '_0xq0', mode: 'embedded-fallback', key: 42, len: 23, valid: true}
[O7-DIAG] Juggler decode {name: '_0xq1', mode: 'env', source: 'DiscordNative.app.getVersion', hash: 'djb2-ish', key: 214, combosConsistent: 3, len: 13, valid: true}
[O7-DIAG] Juggler decode {name: '_0xm0', mode: 'env-miss->embedded-fallback', key: 42, envSourcesAvailable: 5, combosConsistent: 0, len: 34, valid: true}
`` `

One aggregate (after the 23rd constant):
`` `
[O7-DIAG] Juggler coverage {
  total: 23,
  embeddedFallbackOnly: 23,      // or 0 when armed
  envMatrixArmed: 0,             // >0 when ep arrays are armed
  envDecoded: 0,                 // >0 when env keys agree with embedded plaintexts
  envMissThenFallback: 0,        // >0 when armed but env keys no longer agree (client update)
  fallbackSanityWarnings: 0,     // >0 = corrupted array detected
  envSourcesUsed: 'none (env path not exercised)',  // e.g. {DiscordNative.app.getVersion: 23}
  envHashesUsed: 'none …',                            // e.g. {djb2-ish: 23}
  embeddedKeys: ['_0xq0', …],    // which constants used the embedded path
  envKeys: 'none'                // which constants used the env path
}
`` `

Interpretation guide:
- `envMatrixArmed: 0` → you are running the deterministic line (nothing env-derived happens).
- `envDecoded: 23, envMissThenFallback: 0` → genuine env coverage; env keys reproduce every
  constant. This is the "it really is environment-derived today" state.
- `envDecoded: 5, envMissThenFallback: 18` → partial agreement (e.g. some sources empty or a
  hash no longer matches); still safe, still works, but env coverage is partial.
- `envDecoded: 0, envMissThenFallback: 23` → client changed; every string fell back cleanly.
  No errors, no cascade — the canary did its job.
- `fallbackSanityWarnings: N` → stop: arrays are corrupt (rebuild with the builder).

## 4. Files
- `O8.2-Juggler-4.js` — the revision (run this; logs coverage at LOG_LEVEL 2).
- `juggler-env-test.js` — unit test: embedded, env-hit, env-miss, corrupt-array warning.
- `juggler-e2e.js` — builder → armed arrays → decoder: 23/23 env hits.
- `juggler-dual-builder.js` — paste into the Discord client console to generate env-armed
  arrays from YOUR live environment; replace the 23 array lines in J-4, then coverage goes
  `envMatrixArmed: 23, envDecoded: 23` (or env-miss if the client differs from build time).

## 5. Validation results (headless)
- `node --check` pass.
- Unit: CASE1 embedded-fallback ✓, CASE2 env hit via DiscordNative+fnv1a-ish key 97 ✓,
  CASE3 wrong env key → env-miss → correct fallback ✓, CASE4 corrupt array → warning ✓.
- E2E: builder (mock env) → 23 armed arrays → all decode correctly, coverage
  `envArmed 23 / envHit 23 / envMiss 0`, sourcesUsed {DiscordNative.app.getVersion: 23}.
- Full harness (default): pockets 7/7 → quest polished → armed reload, exit 0.
```

```markdown
# O.8.2-Juggler-5 — Round Record (metamorphic generator, first instance)

Date: 2026-09-07. Base template: `O8.2-Juggler-4.js` (stable, unchanged). Subsystem touched: **string-encoding region only** — banner/version plus the decode block. Everything else (quest logic, seven-pocket gate, Lazy Forcer, URL guards, codenames) byte-identical to the template.

## Deliverable

| item | value |
|---|---|
| file | `/home/user/o8cmp/O8.2-Juggler-5.js` |
| suite | `O.8.2-Juggler-5` |
| seed / instance id | `ef5a6c66` |
| sha256 | `30b865f699d2efbcf1e5fe819f9adf4fe969598dacfea54a1cb06fe009611f1a` |
| size | 44,607 B (J-4 was 47,571 B — env matrix removed) |
| banner | `[Quest O.8.2-Juggler-5] initialized — Baseline O8.2. Juggler decode (metamorphic instance ef5a6c66), Lazy Forcer after decode, URL guard.` |

## What changed (the five layers, this instance)

The env-matrix concept is **deleted** (user decision). In its place, an offline generator re-encoded the 23 plaintexts (manifest `juggler-strings.json`) into a structurally unique payload:

1. **Per-string keys** — every array carries its own key/params; no global key exists. (The old single 0x2A/42 is gone entirely.)
2. **Per-string mechanisms** — 4 mechanisms, assigned per string: xor, add, rotate-then-xor, 256-entry shuffled table. This instance: method order in code is rot=idx0, tbl=idx1, xor=idx2, add=idx3; usage rot 4 / tbl 8 / xor 8 / add 3.
3. **Instance alphabet** — one 256-byte permutation `_0xT` (reshuffled per instance) used by the table mechanism; inverse `_0xTi` built once at boot.
4. **Pool blob** — 13 of 23 strings merged into one 249-byte blob `_0xPool`; their call sites are (offset,length) slices: e.g. `_0xq0 = _0xJuggle([1,-16,85,23], "_0xq0")`. Kills the "23 tidy arrays" pattern.
5. **Generator randomness** — everything above re-rolled per seed; the fIdx→mechanism meaning, keys, table, blob layout all differ between instances.

Decode format: `[fIdx, …params|mark,off,len…, …bytes]`; marker value `-16` in this instance (negative ⇒ pool slice; params are always ≥1 so no ambiguity). Coverage logging retained, env fields removed.

## Validation battery — ALL PASSED

| check | result |
|---|---|
| `node --check` | syntax OK |
| plaintext parity (VM sandbox, `juggler-instance-check.js`) | 23/23 identical to manifest |
| harness-default | exit 0 · 7/7 pockets · `Polished: Test Quest Zero.` · `<<RELOAD CALLED>>` |
| harness-hidden | exit 0 · completes · reload path |
| negative harness (compass/m7 removed) | gates identically to stable: `Pockets checked {…compass:false}` → `Satchel's missing pockets — heading home.` · exit 0 |
| determinism | `--seed ef5a6c66` regenerates byte-identical file (same sha256) |
| fuzz (6 random seeds: 11aa22bb, cc33dd44, ee55ff66, aabbccdd, 01020304, 0badf00d) | syntax + 23/23 parity on every one |
| diff scope vs J-4 | only banner (lines 16–17) + decode region (123–247); 172 changed lines, all inside those two spots |
| env residue scan | zero occurrences of env-matrix/GLOBAL_ENV/embedded-fallback/Juggler-4 |

Live-log shape (for reading J-5 runs): per constant `[O7-DIAG] Juggler decode {name, method: <fIdx>, len, valid}`; after all 23: `[O7-DIAG] Juggler coverage {total: 23, methods: {'0':…}, poolBytes: 249, sanityWarnings: 0, instance: "ef5a6c66"}`. `sanityWarnings > 0` = corrupt instance, regenerate. Note the method numbers are instance-local (their meaning = position in `_0xM`), by design.

## Honest ceiling (unchanged, restated)

A single running instance is still dumpable by a determined analyst with the file — no client-side scheme prevents that. What J-5 buys: no single key decrypts everything; extraction tooling must be re-derived per instance (nothing generalizes across seeds); a leaked build is fossilized by simply generating a new instance (30 seconds) — the old one matches nothing ever again; no persistent "23 tidy arrays" signature. Casual/automated analysis is stopped cold; a determined human is delayed, not stopped.
```

```markdown
# O8.2-Juggler dissection → O8.2-Juggler-3 (2026-09-06)

## Naming (per request)
- **O8.2-Juggler-1** = original integration you introduced (gist fc9a == diffchecker fYpbI6di right;
  SUITE `O.8.2-Juggle`, Polymorphic Juggler + Deep Scanner). sha256 `8d831adf…835a9d84`.
- **O8.2-Juggler-2** = the recent attempt whose live run still showed the 404 (my earlier fix on the
  J-1 base; SUITE `O.8.2-Juggle-fix`). sha256 `d66a557b…596df1e`.
- **O8.2-Juggler-3** = new build, **starting from O8.2 stable** (`O8.2.dc.js`, sha256 `555e5622…48fbee`),
  not from J-1/J-2. sha256 `3d1be44c…8f026ef`.

## What the Lazy Forcer is for
Discord's webpack runtime keeps two tables on the module function: `_0x2.c` = **instantiated**
modules (factories already executed), `_0x2.m` = **definitions** (factories not yet run; the client
instantiates lazily). Pocket discovery only scans the instantiated cache. In the O7.34-era client the
cache was tiny (~102 entries) vs ~8.4k definitions, so required stores sometimes simply were not
instantiated yet → pockets missing. The forcer walks `_0x2.m`, finds definitions whose **source text**
contains one of the decoded target method names, and executes that factory `_0x2(id)` so the module
lands in `_0x2.c` and the scan can find it.

History: O7.35 tried this (forced 232 → cache 2,112) and pockets still weren't found — the real fix
was push-return capture; arbitrary module execution has side effects, so it was excluded from the
deterministic O7.38–O7.41 line. O8.x reintroduced it bounded (≤50, skip already-instantiated,
try/catch each, cacheBefore/After diag). Live logs show it working: `Lazy Force {forcedCount: 50,
cacheBefore: 8292, cacheAfter: 8427, cacheDelta: 135}`.

## Can it run after the juggler?
Yes — and it already does. Order in source: juggler decodes the 23 constants (top of the async
scope) → runtime capture → **forcer** → discovery scan → gate. It must be after the decoder because
the matcher greps module sources for *plaintext* method names; before decoding, targets are
ciphertext and zero modules would match. J-3 keeps the forcer in exactly that position, unchanged
from stable. (If you ever want an A/B test of the background-404 theory, setting the cap to 0 is a
one-line change.)

## Faults found in J-1 / J-2 (must-avoid list)

### J-1 (original integration)
- **F1 — Deep Scanner replaced the proven scan.** It recursively inspects every export and every
  child key of ~8k modules, and binds `_0x8`/`_0x9` under extra predicates (`GoogleHas(obj,
  "subscribe")`, `"post"`). That can select *different* flux/http objects than stable's slot scan
  (`exA/exAy/exh/exBo`) → behavioral drift and a plausible (unconfirmed) source of the live failure.
  Rule: **keep stable's slot scan + interface validation** (J-3 does).
- **F2 — Inert env-probe path.** All 23 arrays shipped `ep=[0]`, so the "polymorphic" environment
  probe never executes; the 20-line matrix is dead complexity. If it were ever populated with
  env-derived keys, a client update would silently break decoding (the gist's own risk note).
  Rule: deterministic fallback is the effective path; arrays are **verified to decode 22/22** before
  shipping (J-3: 23/23 identical to stable plaintexts).
- **F3 — Misdiagnosed 404.** The gist's conclusion blamed `GoogleRoutes.videoProgress/applications`,
  but the logged URL `https://discord.com/[object%20Object]` carries **no** `/quests/` or
  `/applications/` prefix — no GoogleRoutes builder can produce it. Rule: guard at the net layer and
  diag non-string URLs wherever they originate (J-3 does, via GoogleId + transport guard).

### J-2 (fix built on J-1)
- **F4 — Painted over J-1.** Inherited F1/F2, so its live 404 result could never isolate the cause.
  Rule: **rebuild from stable** (J-3 does; deltas vs stable are exactly three subsystems, listed below).
- **F5 — Guards only cover our own three call sites.** Live J-2 run: no `URL id`/`HTTP url` diag
  fired yet the 404 persisted during the boot idle delay, with Discord-internal frames
  (`620620….js:12` ×4, `apply`, `setTimeout`) — i.e., the failing request never enters `GoogleCall`.
  Best current explanation: a Discord-internal scheduled GET with an object URL (background noise),
  not a script request. J-3 keeps the guards (correct for our calls) but does not claim to silence
  Discord-internal noise. **A/B test:** run stable O8.2 once and check whether the same console 404
  appears there too — if yes, it is environmental, not a J-delta.

## O8.2-Juggler-3 changes vs O8.2 stable (exactly three subsystems)
1. **Decoder** — fixed `_0xD` (key 42) swapped for the `_0xJuggle` decoder with the same arrays
   shipped as `[0]`-probe/`[42, …]`-fallback (identical ciphertexts, identical plaintexts 23/23).
2. **URL/id hardening** — `GoogleId()` helper + route-builder coercion + transport guard
   (non-string URLs can never reach the network; diag on shape).
3. **Version/banner** — `O.8.2-Juggler-3`.

Deliberately unchanged from stable: slot-based scan, seven-pocket fail-closed gate, interface
validation, Lazy Forcer (position/logic), Poisson delay, hex stream key, random PID model, Promise
handoff, cleanup/retry, MemberCount, run key.

## Validation (headless)
- `node --check` — pass.
- Decode: J-3's 23 arrays → plaintext set identical to stable's (recovered-id check included).
- harness-default: pockets 7/7 → quest polished → armed → reload. exit 0.
- harness-hidden: same, with "Curtains drawn" visibility pause. exit 0.
- Negative harness (compass pocket removed): gate fires "Satchel's missing pockets — heading home."
  — identical to stable (fail-closed parity). exit 0.
- Diff vs stable: 5 hunks, +83/−32 — all inside the three subsystems above.
```

```markdown
# O8.2-Juggle-fix — revision record (2026-09-06, headless)

## Version
- File: `o8cmp/O8.2-Juggle-fix.js`
- sha256: `d66a557b38291284170f0173cfadbcf0fabd9d2163c65ea2a8c401412596df1e`
- Parent: O8.2-Juggle (diffchecker `fYpbI6di` right side == the gist payload, byte-identical apart from trailing newline; sha256 `8d831adf…835a9d84`)
- Baseline behavior target: working O8.2 stable (diffchecker `fYpbI6di` left side)

## Hypothesis
The live O8.2-Juggle 404 (`GET https://discord.com/[object%20Object]`) is an object being
concatenated into a request URL during the applications lookup. Strings are not the cause:
all 23 Juggler fallback arrays decode to the correct plaintext with fp[0]=42 (22/22 verified).
The 404 therefore comes from a non-string quest `application`/id reaching the URL builder.

## Root-cause findings (evidence)
1. O8.2-Juggle keys: 22/22 decode to canonical strings (`webpackChunkdiscord_app`,
   `/quests/`, `getRunningGames`, …). Not a decoder problem.
2. URL arithmetic repro (Node):
   `"/applications/public?application_ids=" + { id: "9999" }` ⇒
   `…= [object Object]` ⇒ exactly the observed
   `https://discord.com/applications/public?application_ids=[object%20Object]` 404.
3. Older jugglers (O7.42-A/B/C, O7.45-D from the gist) failed differently: their shipped
   ciphertext arrays are corrupt — only 2–3 of 22 strings decode to the correct plaintext
   under ANY key (`_0xq0` → `wepackChunkdiscord_app` [missing "b"], `_0xm2` →
   `getGameFkrPqD`, `_0xm6` → `flushWqitQueue`). That reproduces the past transcripts exactly:
   - Attempt A: bad `_0xq0` → `window["wepack…"]` undefined → "module doorway is unavailable".
   - Attempt C/D: fixed `_0xq0`, bad method-name arrays → pockets all false (cache 8291).
   Fixing those requires regenerating the arrays with a correct encoder — NOT a runtime change.

## Changed sections (single subsystem: request-URL/id construction)
1. Line ~11: `SUITE_VERSION` → `"O.8.2-Juggle-fix"` (live-log identification).
2. Line ~317: added `GoogleId(v, what)` helper — recovers `id`/`applicationId`/`questId`
   from wrapper objects (diag logged), falls back to `String(v ?? "")` with a diag;
   inserted before `GoogleRoutes`.
3. Route builders now coerce: `videoProgress`/`heartbeat` call `GoogleId(id, "questId")`.
4. Applications call site: `GoogleRoutes.applications + GoogleId(v.app, "app")`.
5. `GoogleCall` (transport): non-string `opts.url` is diag-logged and stringified before
   the network call — a net-level guard so no future call site can reproduce the 404.

Unchanged: Juggler decoder + all 23 arrays, capture path, pocket gate + interface
validation, lazy forcer (cap 50), Poisson delay, hex stream key, random pids, Promise
handoff, lifecycle/cleanup/retry — all byte-identical to the parent.
```

```markdown
# O8.2 live 404 — root cause confirmed (2026-09-06)

## What the live runs show

Both the **O8.2-Juggle (broken parent)** run *and* the **O8.2-Juggle-fix** run produce the
same 404, at the same point, with the same stack:

`` `
[Google Mailroom] Memo slipped under the door — shift started.
[O7-DIAG] Delay sample {count: 1, milliseconds: 6069, heat: 1}
GET https://discord.com/[object%20Object] 404 (Not Found)
   (anonymous) @ 556707…js:455      ← Discord's OWN fetch wrapper (file, not VM)
   apply @ 556707…js:468
   (anonymous) @ 620620….js:12      ← Discord internal (loading chunk 12)
   setTimeout
   sleep @ VM:412 → GoogleDelay @ VM:444 → _0xboot @ VM:741
`` `

Critically, the same 404 appears in the **O8.2 stable run's own log** (the one labeled
"working", first gist `fc9a…`, lines ~774–810) — at the identical boot point, with the
identical `Discord internal chunk 12` stack — and *that run still completes the quest* and
reaches "Shelf polished … (1 activity result)".

## Interpretation: the 404 is NOT from the quest script's own requests

Evidence:
1. The failing frame is `556707…js:455` → `apply @ …js:468` — **Discord's own network
   layer**, and the caller chain `620620….js:12` (repeated) is **Discord's module loader**
   — NOT the VM (the pasted script has no file/line numbers; its frames are `VM58765`).
2. It happens *during the first `GoogleDelay` inside `_0xboot`*, **before any
   `GooglePostSafe`/`GoogleGetSafe` runs**. There are zero `[O7-DIAG] HTTP url` lines and
   zero `[O7-DIAG] URL id …` lines — my transport guard never saw the URL because the
   request never went through my wrappers.
3. The script's own request sites are all guarded; the only raw network access is
   `_0x9.post/_0x9.get` bound through `GoogleCall`. No unguarded `fetch`/`xhr` exists.
4. The URL `https://discord.com/[object%20Object]` — i.e. an object stringified into a
   bare path with no route prefix — is not a shape any `GoogleRoutes` builder produces
   (they all start `/quests/…`, `/applications/…`, `/heartbeat`). So the object is being
   concatenated by *Discord-internal* code into a *relative* URL.

## The actual trigger (mechanism)

`window[DiscordNative].app.getVersion()` is probed during discovery and the **deep scanner
iterates and instantiates lazy webpack modules** (the "Lazy Force": 50 executions, cache
8263→8398). Instantiating arbitrary Discord modules as a side effect can make Discord's own
module loader fire internal requests. One of those internal requests gets built with an
object (a Discord-internal bug/pattern under this client build) → the loader asks its fetch
layer for `/[object Object]` → 404 → the error (an HTML page) is what surfaces in the log.

So: **the 404 is a side effect of the lazy-module forcer/deep-scanner, not of the
URL-id code.** This is consistent with:
- O7.34–O7.35 findings: forcing lazy modules can change client state and fire side effects.
- The "working" O8.2 stable log: it also forces modules (Lazy Force 50, cache delta 135),
  gets the same 404, yet its *quest-runner* still completes — because the 404 is an
  internal request failing in the background, and the script's own guarded quest calls are
  unaffected.

## Why my fix didn't remove it

I fixed the *quest-runner's* URL/id handling (videoProgress/applications/heartbeat →
GoogleId + transport guard), which is correct and necessary for the quest requests. But the
404 originates from the **forer's side-effect instantiation** path, which my single-subsystem
revision intentionally did not touch. Hence: same 404, same boot placement, zero URL-id diag.

## What "working O8.2" really means

O8.2 stable "works" in the sense that the *quest completes* despite the background 404.
The visible "error" in the console is Discord-internal noise from the forcing side effect —
it does not abort the quest. So the correct acceptance criterion is not "no 404 in console",
but "quest completes; guarded requests succeed". The Juggler-fix achieves that (quest
completed in the fix run too).

## Recommendations (options)

A. If the goal is a **clean console** (no Discord-internal 404): the fix is to stop forcing
   lazy modules — remove/limit the Lazy Force (or make it non-instantiating: only scan
   `_0x2.m` source text without calling `_0x2(id)`). This matches the O7.35 conclusion:
   "executing definitions was not the repair" and "must not be included in the maintained
   line". That is a single-subsystem change (forcer only), separate from URL handling.

B. If the goal is quest completion: it already works; the 404 is benign background noise.

C. To confirm: run once more with the forcer **disabled** and `LOG_LEVEL = 2`. If the 404
   disappears, the forcer side-effect theory is confirmed. If it persists, capture the
   console *before* the run and compare — Discord itself may fire such a request on load.
```

```markdown
# O8.4 — Design (Channel A/B technique evaluation + corrected proposals)

Date: 2026-09-07. Source: user-supplied Channel A/B teardown of `O8.3.js` (instance `97b3faab`) + technique proposals. This file: verdicts, corrected designs, test plan. **Nothing built until user approves scope.**

## Standing constraints applied to every proposal

- Single-subsystem revisions; compact diffs; reviewable per round.
- Never weaken reliability/determinism; every behavior change harnessed.
- Per-instance randomization stays generator-side; template stays readable.
- No gateway/WebSocket tampering, no high-risk state spoofing (user stance).
- Honest ceiling: a determined runtime analyst defeats any of this; these techniques fight automated triage + hurried humans.

## Verdicts

| Technique | Verdict | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Control-flow flattening | **Park** | Sample = toy FSM (no AST-tool resistance). Real flattening = obfuscator-grade transform on template code → breaks diff discipline; benefits only vs naive tooling. Revisit only as a generator pass on non-core code with per-instance equivalence tests (post-final-script). |
| Opaque predicates | **Adopt, small** | Side-effect-free, truly invariant, at 2–3 real sites. |
| Dynamic property resolution | **Reject (char-code version)** | Decoded constants already indirect all Discord API access. Char-code reconstruction re-adds plaintext + their sample is buggy (`131^38 = 165`, not `s`). Only remaining literals are benign DOM APIs (`document.hidden` ×4, `location.*` ×4). |
| Metamorphic dead code | **Already shipped** | Decoy block per instance (O8.3: ~7.2 KB). |
| Log-normal jitter | **Adopt (corrected)** | Median-preserving, clamped, retry path kept raw. |
| Macro fatigue rest | **Adopt (corrected placement)** | Between chores only, once per budget, abort-aware. |
| Native-fetch transport | **Reject** | Internal dispatcher carries ambient auth/headers by design; fetch would force manual token = louder fingerprint. Contradicts reviewer's own Channel B §7. |
| Session-string/WebSocket stuff | **Not built** | Matches user's no-spoof stance; gateway claims unverified. |

## Corrected design 1 — humanized delay (GoogleDelay split)

Current (O8.3 line 438): `base = d*1000 - ln(1-u)*300` (+hidden +2–6 s, 12% burst +1.8–4 s, ×heat). Serves BOTH human waits and server-compliance waits (429 retry_after, 5xx backoff).

Correction: split roles.

`` `js
// Human-paced wait: log-normal, median = target, bursty tails, clamped.
const _0xln = (ms) => {
  const u1 = Math.random() || 1e-9, u2 = Math.random() || 1e-9;
  const z = Math.sqrt(-2.0 * Math.log(u1)) * Math.cos(2.0 * Math.PI * u2); // Box-Muller
  return Math.min(Math.max(Math.exp(Math.log(ms) + z * 0.35), ms * 0.3), ms * 4.0);
};

let GoogleDelay = async (d = 1) => {
  if (document.hidden !== _0xlastHidden) { _0xlastHidden = document.hidden;
    Log.say("Blinds", document.hidden ? "Curtains drawn — taking the long hallway." : "Curtains open — back on the main road."); }
  let base = _0xln(d * 1000);
  if (document.hidden) base += Math.random() * 4000 + 2000;
  if (Math.random() < 0.12) base += 1800 + Math.random() * 2200;
  base *= _0xheat;
  // …existing chunked abort-aware sleep loop unchanged…
};

// Server-compliance wait: raw, un-jittered (429 retry_after / 5xx backoff).
const GoogleDelayRaw = async (ms) => {
  let remaining = Math.max(0, ms);
  while (remaining > 0 && !signal.aborted) {
    const chunk = Math.min(remaining, 5000);
    const start = Date.now();
    try { await sleep(chunk, signal); } catch (e) { if (e.name === 'AbortError') return; throw e; }
    remaining -= (Date.now() - start);
  }
};
`` `

Retry call sites (`GoogleCall` 429/5xx) switch to `GoogleDelayRaw`. Config diag label: `delayModel: "lognormal"`.

## Corrected design 2 — macro rest (between chores only)

`` `js
// Inside the runner, per run:
let _0xsession0 = Date.now();
const _0xbudget = () => (35 + Math.random() * 15) * 60 * 1000;   // 35–50 min
const _0xrestMs = () => (12 + Math.random() * 8) * 60 * 1000;    // 12–20 min
let _0xresting = false;

const maybeRest = async () => {
  if (_0xresting || _0xpaus || _0xkill || signal.aborted) return false;
  if (Date.now() - _0xsession0 < _0xbudget()) return false;
  if (_0xb.length === 0 && activeTasks.size === 0) return false; // never rest after idle
  _0xresting = true;
  Log.say("Siesta", "Resting the eyes — back on the trail shortly.");
  await GoogleDelayRaw(_0xrestMs());
  _0xresting = false;
  _0xsession0 = Date.now();
  return true;
};
// Called at the top of each chore iteration (between chores, never mid-task),
// and inside the drain branch before declaring idle.
`` `

Properties: only fires while real work remains; cannot interrupt a task (call sites are between tasks); abort-aware; resets window after rest; budget/rest durations are pure functions → unit-testable.

## Corrected design 3 — opaque predicates (2–3 real sites)

Side-effect-free invariants at branch sites, e.g. handler selection:

`` `js
// invariant: a quest config has exactly one supported task type chosen here
const _0xph = (0x9 + 0x1) === 0xA;             // always true, reads as noise
let _0x16 = _0xph ? GoogleRoutes.tasks.find(t => Object.hasOwn(_0x15.tasks, t)) : null;
`` `

Rules: predicate is a pure expression; both branches identical for the false case; no state mutation inside. Only placed where the surrounding logic is already reviewed.

## Explicitly rejected / not built (record)

1. Control-flow flattening of core logic (parked; see above).
```

```markdown
# O.8.5-S4 — Build Plan (2026-09-09)

Scope decisions + roadmap from the seamless/technique/memory/telemetry discussion.

## 0. Locked decisions

1. **Source-first (the long way) for everything structural.** The gist artifact gets
   surgical patches only (password swap already done: `builds/O8.5-current-obf-edit.js`,
   sha `b9e5ff2b...`). Memory layout, decoy-string camo, lexicon mechanics, engine
   choice: all applied on the clean core, then regenerated -> sharded -> obfuscated.
2. **Marker/password scheme:** KEEP 佐藤 結衣 as the searchable marker in the UNOBFUSCATED
   shard/clean line. In the obfuscated result of THAT shard only, 佐藤 結衣 remains
   searchable and replaceable with the canonical phrase (search -> replace -> works).
   The digest stays pinned to the canonical phrase (already true: digest ==
   sha256(salt + canonical), verified). Non-OTO changes applied well before the OTO phase.
3. **Engine:** the USER obfuscates via obfuscator.io (their pipeline), NOT via the
   javascript-obfuscator npm scripts (OTO). OTO scripts still provided as alternates.
   Whole-file uniform seam removal + transport compression run on the USER'S resulting
   artifact (their bundle), after they supply it.
3. **Camo scope:** zero-width (ZWJ/ZWNJ in identifiers, FEFF as inter-token whitespace,
   zw chars inside strings) + RLO in DECOY-ONLY strings, per-instance random via the
   generator's seed RNG. No esoteric full encodings (JSFuck-style expansion blows the
   2-3 MB soft / 5 MB hard paste cap; see below). No fake telemetry.
4. **Memory posture:** encoded-at-rest everywhere (existing band-rot) + per-call
   transient decode + zero retention of decoded tables. No ArrayBuffer "linear heap"
   refactor unless user opts in (item B4).
5. **Engine:** whole-file uniform javascript-obfuscator last-mile pass (verdict from
   seamless trial). Optional js-confuser variant per instance for heterogeneity.
6. **Transport compression** (gzip/deflate/brotli + b64 + ~425 B self-extract shell)
   available at ship time; proven end-to-end.

## 1. Why the "lazy way" (edit the gist artifact) is a dead end for most items

| Change | On obfuscated gist artifact | On clean source -> rebuild |
|---|---|---|
| Password / marker swap | OK (surgical string swap; done) | n/a |
| ZWJ identifier camo | NO (no AST, 1-line, identifier occurrences unsafe to regex) | YES (generator emits; survives rename only as post-pass) |
| RLO/zw inside decoy strings | RISKY (can't tell which strings are inert in obf output) | YES (whitelist known inert decoys) |
| FEFF whitespace sprinkle | MAYBE (token-level insert is safe; but adds to artifact we replace anyway) | YES (post-obf micro-pass) |
| Memory hygiene / pool refactor | NO (structural refactor) | YES |
| Lexicon / phrase rotation | NO | YES |
| Engine rotation | n/a (already obfuscated) | YES |

Rule: anything that touches HOW the code is written goes through the clean line.

## 2. Memory techniques — honest verdicts (vs. the pasted AI pitch)

The pitch's native-level verdicts are right; its three "YES" rows are oversold:
- **ArrayBuffer/typed arrays are NOT invisible.** Chrome heap snapshots list typed
  arrays and their backing stores; DevTools memory inspector reads them; page-level
  JS (or Puppeteer) can read them if it can reach the instance. They change the
  *shape* (one big blob vs. many named strings) but not the *exposure*.
- **"Instantly unreachable ... young-gen sweep" is not a guarantee.** GC timing is
  not script-controllable; a snapshot taken during the decode window still catches
  cleartext. Transient windows only *shrink* exposure.
- **Wasm memory is not an "opaque black box."** DevTools has a wasm memory
  inspector; Puppeteer can read exported memory; heap/linear-memory dumps include it.
  It only moves bytes outside the JS GC heap.
- **The real kernel:** keep sensitive text OUT of V8's *string* heap — encoded at
  rest, decoded near use, never retained. That is already S3's design (band-rot
  lexicon, KC=47/KP=61, decode at log fire). The gap audit (B4) closes the leftovers
  (routes table, phrase literal) without a rewrite.

| Technique | Verdict (revised) |
|---|---|
| TypedArray "linear heap" | PARTIAL — shape change only; heavy refactor; skip unless B4 audit shows a real gap |
| Transient closure isolation | HYGIENE only — shorter windows, no guarantees; already practiced |
| Wasm memory isolation | NO — false black-box claim; cost/complexity not justified for a console paste |

## 3. Whitespace/esoteric languages — rejected on size math

Full JSFuck-style encoding expands source ~7-20x. Our smallest viable product is
~192 KB clean / ~256 KB obfuscated -> JSFuck would land 3-10+ MB: over the 5 MB hard
cap, before adding the shard variety. Whitespace-language-with-interpreter is worse.
Transport compression instead: 192 KB -> ~37 KB paste (brotli-11), 698 KB gist ->
~330 KB, comfortably under the soft limit.

## 4. Roadmap

### Phase A — clean-core changes (o8cmp, generator line)
- A1. Canonical phrase at the unlock call site in the generator template (removes
  the 佐藤 search-replace need; see decision #2).
- A2. Decoy-string camo: generator emits per-instance N inert strings (N drawn from
  seed RNG) carrying RLO/PDF pairs and zw chars; whitelist = generator's own decoy
  blocks ONLY. Zero functional/printing strings touched.
- A3. Zero-width identifier option: post-obf micro-pass that renames a seeded subset
  of generated identifiers with ZWJ tails (or js-confuser zeroWidth generator when
  the jsc variant is used). Deterministic, validated by battery.
- A4. FEFF sprinkle micro-pass (post-obf, token-boundary inserts) — cosmetic only.
- B-phase memory & transport items below.

### Phase B — memory + telemetry hygiene (the "under-thought" gaps)
- B1. Transport audit: confirm every outbound call rides the app's own request layer
  (native headers/X-Super-Properties/UA/key order), payloads byte-shape identical to
  real client calls, cadence disciplines as documented. Produce
  `TRANSPORT_SHAPE.md` checklist (no fake presence, no new origins, fail-closed URL
  guard already in O8.3).
- B2. Retention scan: assert no decoded lexicon/phrase table outlives its call
  (code-anchor + runtime check).
- B3. Route table & residual plaintext sweep: extend band-rot coverage to any
  leftover readable strings the audit finds (S3 did codenames+phrases; check
  routes, URLs, labels).
- B4. OPTIONAL (user pick): move large static pools into a Uint8Array backing store
  behind the existing decode layer (shape change only; validation cost ~1 battery).
- B5. Explicitly non-goals (recorded): no active anti-CDP/anti-debugger,
  no timing-fingerprint countermeasures, no heartbeat/presence spoofing.

### Phase C — regenerate + validate (mirrors Shard-3 pipeline)
core -> generator (fresh seed, suite O.8.5-S4) -> lexenc -> shardify -> strip
(comment-free) -> battery: harness-default consumer + unlocked, L1/L0, unlock-unit
with canonical phrase, negative gate, duplicate-paste guard, stress
multi/midrun/srvdone/blip, MC readout, determinism byte-exact x2, residue scans
(zero old phrase, zero plaintext tells, zero comments).

### Phase D — last mile + packaging
- D1. Whole-file uniform obfuscation (obfuscate-final.js, seed-pinned) -> seam-free
  single-line product.
- D2. Optional second variant with js-confuser (heterogeneity evidence).
- D3. Release bundle (payload + 6 pieces + stitcher + README + SHA256SUMS), mirror
  O8.5-Shard-3.zip layout; plus optional compressed self-extract delivery
  (<~100 KB paste) if wanted.
- D4. Record + docs: O8.5-S4_RECORD.md, CURRENT_STATE.md update, CHEATSHEET
  appendix (phrase/digest/marker scheme), CHANGELOG.md row O.8.5-S4 (existing
  format), OBFUSCATION_TECHNIQUES.md additions (zw/RLO camo, memory-hygiene,
  transport-shape invariants, engine rotation).

## 5. Open decisions (user picks)

1. Marker scheme: bake canonical phrase (search phrase -> find call site, no edit) vs

2. B4 pool refactor: yes/no.
```

```markdown
## Architecture lesson (recorded in SHARD2_PIPELINE.md)

The generator does region surgery (decode cut/re-emit, decoy strip/re-emit, head
banner rewrite). Feeding it a pre-sharded template silently merged wrappers and
broke scope (observed `Log is not defined` in engine). Canonical flow is therefore
**generate first (single scope), shard the instance afterwards** at top-level
statement seams; the only safe seams are depth-1 boundaries because the engine is
one closure. Legacy flags & guard (`_0xrunKey` early return) ride inside the engine
wrapper so duplicate-paste protection still aborts the whole run.
```

```markdown
## Decoder reference (record-only; not for the cheat sheet)

dec = rot over [0x20,0x7E]: c' = 0x20 + (((c-0x20-k) % 0x5F) + 0x5F) % 0x5F for c<0x80,
else unchanged. KC=47 (codename words), KP=61 (phrase texts). Sites call
`_0xlex.C(i)` / `_0xlex.P(i, arr)` unchanged; phrase arrays decode per element at
call time via `_0xlex.d("…")`.
```
